short: ASR decoding (M06) and phoneme LM (M07) on heard-speech ECoG: standard, with ECoG precedents of 2015. Electrodes chosen on the test set (M12); LM effect not isolated from smoothing.
position: The paper changes the decoder (M06) and language model (M07) of heard-speech ECoG decoding [@moses2016]: LDA likelihoods, a phoneme 4-gram and Viterbi search over multi-lag high-gamma windows (HGWs). Both are standard: the same ASR chain ran on ECoG in two 2015 reports from one group [@herff2015; @heger2015], the first cited by the authors, and multi-lag features predate it in their own group [@pasley2012]; the priority claim rests on its "single-speaker" qualifier (§1). Against the usual design then, closed-set classification of segmented trials (8 of 18 prior decoders, Appendix), continuous phoneme output from heard speech is the real step. The strongest confound: electrodes were chosen on the whole Gump set later cross-validated (§2.1.4). The LM's contribution is not isolated: no zero-weight decoding is reported (§2.2.3), and the authors credit the gain to temporal smoothing (§4). The best neural PER, 70.47%, pools averaged responses of three subjects (Table 5), infeasible for a prosthesis by the authors' account (§4).
